items.text: Trump's deportation crackdown "might be too tough," the president said on 60 Minutes, adding a deal with Democrats on long-term immigrants is "doable."
items.detail: In the interview, taped Friday and aired Sunday on CBS, Trump said the crackdown "both helped and hurt" and that "we also took people that had good jobs." Asked whether the policy was too tough, he said, "I think it might be too tough, yeah." He described a possible deal that would deport "the killers," "the rough ones" and "the drug dealers" while letting people who have been "here for ten and 15 years" stay, said Democrats had "already called me," and acknowledged some in his administration want everyone removed. No bill, order or formal proposal exists. About an hour after the taping, per CBS, Trump named Stephen Miller, an immigration hardliner, White House chief of staff; Miller starts Monday. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said, "That's not a course correction. That's a promotion." Trump also said countries protected by U.S. escorts in the Strait of Hormuz "are going to pay us back any and all costs that we've had for the war," without giving a figure.
items.why: It is the first sign the president may soften his signature policy after Democrats won Congress.

items.text: Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation after reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
items.detail: The board said Sunday a committee of independent directors, advised by outside independent counsel, will investigate the reporting; it said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised," that it has confidence in Huang, and that he will remain CEO and cooperate. In an email to employees, Huang wrote, "I was unfaithful to my wife," apologized, and said, "I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security." AP, citing The New York Times, said Huang had told the board of a relationship with a business executive whom U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing. China's Foreign Ministry called the spying claim groundless. Nvidia shares fell about 4% to 5% in premarket trading Monday, CNBC reported. The company reports earnings Nov. 17.
items.why: It puts a national-security question over the head of the leading maker of AI chips.

items.text: U.S.-China trade truce measures were extended by both sides, with China keeping its extra 24% tariff on U.S. goods suspended for two more months.
items.detail: China's tariff commission said the 24% additional tariff stays suspended for two months from 1:01 p.m. Beijing time Tuesday, while a 10% extra tariff remains; its transport ministry extended the suspension of special port fees on U.S.-linked ships to Jan. 10, 2027, with its probe on hold. Beijing cited the consensus from the leaders' meeting in September. On the U.S. side, the trade representative extended the pause on Section 301 port fees for Chinese-linked ships and duties on Chinese ship-to-shore cranes and cargo equipment through 11:59 p.m. ET Jan. 9, 2027, "to allow for further discussion with China," and the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security kept its "Affiliates Rule" export-control expansion on hold through Jan. 10, 2027 (Federal Register, Nov. 9).
items.why: It keeps the truce's tariff and shipping-fee pauses from lapsing for importers, exporters and shippers.
items.source: USTR; China's finance ministry (State Council Tariff Commission); Federal Register

items.text: Iraq's Khor Mor gas field stopped production after a suspected drone attack, knocking out power to most of the Kurdistan Region.
items.detail: Operator Dana Gas said production halted after a "suspected" drone attack late Sunday sparked a fire, which was put out; no staff were hurt. The Kurdistan Regional Government's electricity ministry said about 2,800 megawatts of generation went offline, and officials told Al Jazeera more than 70% of the region lost power, with hydro and alternative-fuel plants supplying hospitals and water stations. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered a joint investigation. No group claimed the attack; Kurdish officials have blamed earlier attacks on the field on Iran-backed militias.
items.why: It cut power across most of Iraq's Kurdistan Region amid the regional war.

items.text: Iran talks are not near a breakthrough, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said, calling some Iranian demands "outrageous and ridiculous."
items.detail: Rubio said Sunday before leaving for the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris, "I wouldn't say we're at the verge of a breakthrough," and that Iran's demands were "not just unacceptable, but in some cases outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic." Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran's "2-day proposal stands": on day one the U.S. would end the war on all fronts, lift sanctions, reduce its regional presence and unfreeze assets, and on day two Iran would reopen Hormuz shipping; he said the alternative was war. Trump told CNN renewed strikes were "highly unlikely" if Iran signs "a very strong agreement," said the U.S. has identified targets including 38 bridges, and posted that "Task Force Iron Gate is in full force and effect." Trump meets Qatar's prime minister Monday. Separately, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said Iraq reached understandings with the U.S. to let its oil exports pass through Hormuz via a lane near Oman, Reuters reported.
items.why: It signals no quick end to the war or the Hormuz closure that is lifting energy costs.

items.text: Polish prosecutors opened a terrorism investigation into the Kraków shooting, and officials said four of the six people killed were Polish.
items.detail: The regional governor said the dead were four women and two men: three of the women and one man were Polish, one man was from the United Kingdom and one woman was from Austria. The wounded include citizens of Britain, Portugal, Russia, Germany and Austria. The national prosecutor's office said it is investigating the killing of six people with a firearm and the attempted murder of many others, including police officers. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński, who said Saturday the 24-year-old suspect was drawn to far-right ideologies, said Sunday that was one hypothesis police are checking and that officials are "not passing any verdicts." Police have not publicly named the suspect.
items.why: It narrows what is officially known about the suspect's motive after Saturday's far-right claims.

items.text: Gadi Eisenkot formally received the mandate to form Israel's next government Sunday, starting a 28-day clock to build a coalition of at least 61 seats.
items.detail: President Isaac Herzog handed the Yashar party leader the mandate at the President's Residence in Jerusalem, saying representatives of 67 incoming lawmakers recommended Eisenkot, against 46 for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Herzog may grant up to 14 more days if needed. Eisenkot said Israel is in a state of emergency "approaching a point of no return," called for a "national emergency government" and urged Likud and Religious Zionism lawmakers to join a government under his leadership; Netanyahu has called for a unity government. Likud remains the largest party, and Eisenkot's bloc lacks a clear majority.
items.why: It moves Israel's post-election coalition fight from announcement to a formal deadline that decides whether Netanyahu is replaced.

items.text: Attorney General Todd Blanche said Democratic lawmakers' threats against the administration could be criminal, but he did not announce an investigation or name a crime.
items.detail: Asked on CNN's "State of the Union" whether the Democratic rhetoric was a crime, Blanche said, "It depends on what's said. So yes, there could be," and added that he is not saying every case would be prosecuted. He said he would be "very worried" if he were on the House Oversight Committee, whose incoming chair, Rep. Robert Garcia, told Trump allies to "lawyer up," and that Justice Department lawyers will defend administration officials, including incoming chief of staff Stephen Miller, if oversight turns improper. He said, "I welcome oversight." Garcia has said Democrats "are not going to be intimidated." Saturday, Trump said he was ordering a Justice Department inquiry into Democrats' alleged threats; no investigation has been announced.
items.why: It is the attorney general's first on-air response to Trump's order, days before Democrats take over House oversight.

items.text: Treasury on Friday cut a major crypto exchange off from U.S. banks, saying it moved at least $16 billion in illicit funds, and sanctioned eight Canadian money businesses linked to Iran.
items.detail: FinCEN's order under section 9714 of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act bars U.S. financial institutions from transmitting funds to or from the exchange and takes effect 30 days after Federal Register publication. Treasury said the exchange moved at least $16 billion between May 2021 and May 2026 tied to Iranian, North Korean and Russian sanctions evasion and cybercrime, including about $22 million for Iran's central bank and the IRGC. It does not freeze user assets. Separately, OFAC designated eight Canadian money services businesses that convert Iranian rials into digital assets, some tied to IRGC-linked addresses and to sanctioned Canadian drug trafficker Ryan Wedding's laundering. Both actions were announced Friday as part of Operation Economic Outcast; the exchange has said operations are normal.
items.why: It extends the Iran-war sanctions campaign into crypto channels and a major offshore exchange.

items.text: Poland began two days of national mourning Sunday, and police said the three people found dead at the Kraków gunman's home were his parents and sister.
items.detail: The 24-year-old suspect, who authorities say held far-right, ultranationalist views, is in critical condition in a hospital after police shot him during Saturday's attack, which killed six people and wounded 15 in the Old Town's Main Square. The family home is in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, about 150 kilometers (93 miles) northeast of Kraków, where police said several firearms were seized; he and his father belonged to a shooting club. A British national was among the dead, and the wounded include citizens of Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia. Two police officers who stopped the attacker are hospitalized, one in critical condition. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it far-right terrorism; the square stayed partly sealed off Sunday.
items.why: Officials are treating Poland's rare mass shooting as terrorism as the country takes stock of the dead.

also.text: Medicare's drug price negotiation program was written into a final rule, effective Dec. 5, governing prices from 2029.
also.detail: The CMS final rule (CMS-4215-F), published in the Federal Register Monday, codifies how Medicare negotiates prices for high-cost drugs, starting with the 2029 price year. It sets a policy for fixed-combination drugs and a temporary price floor for qualifying small biotech drugs in 2029 and 2030.
also.why: It locks in the rules for Medicare's price talks on the most costly drugs.
